correctness.rationale: The source update is reconstructed with F=-a, f(x)=sigma*x/(1+x), q(x)=sigma^2*x^2/(1+x)^3. The normal integral is finite iff p*h*q(x)<1, as follows by completing the square. q attains its unique maximum 4 sigma^2/27 at x=2, proving the uniform finite-moment half. For any x0>0, the quadratic-normal first-step map has positive density at 2, since its minimum is <2. At the critical h, delta_p has a quadratic zero with positive Gaussian-linear numerator, producing a nonintegrable exp(c/(x-2)^2) singularity; above it, conditional moments are infinite on an open interval. Jensen gives uniform propagation of infinite moments. Standard globally Lipschitz SDE estimates provide finite exact-solution moments. The bundled standalone code verifies exact coefficient identities and finite Gaussian integral identities.

value.rationale: For a globally Lipschitz positive SDE with bounded smooth coefficient derivatives and finite true moments of every order, the positive first-order numerical scheme can have infinite mathematical p-moments after exactly two steps. The sharp p*h*sigma^2=27/4 safety frontier is a usable structural timestep criterion; the equality and all-initial-state properties cannot be detected from a single deterministic-state integrability check or finite Monte Carlo samples. The saturated per-capita diffusion is a natural smooth nonlinear multiplicative-noise model, not an arbitrary finite table or normalizing example.
